purpose: Security and provenance boundaries for shared human/AI-authored content in collaborative Shine applications.
requirements: Every shared record has an explicit author/source class and visibility/audience boundary.
Untrusted text is escaped or encoded at HTML/export boundaries; stored text is never treated as executable markup by default.
AI-authored or AI-suggested content remains labelled as AI and cannot become approved fact solely because a model produced it.
Approval, truth/classification and audience changes require an authorised human role and are recorded separately from content generation.
Reads, search results, exports and related-record traversal apply the same membership and audience filtering before returning data.
Private provenance, DM-only notes and hidden records do not become searchable side channels for players.
Invitations are bound to explicit accounts, expire, can be cancelled, and membership revocation takes effect on later reads.
Mutation requests are origin/host constrained and request bodies are bounded before parsing.
Session credentials are unpredictable, expiry-bounded, HttpOnly and protected against cross-site browser submission; production transport must additionally use Secure cookies.
Backup/restore input is byte-bounded, schema-validated and restored into a safe review state rather than blindly preserving authority, sharing or approval.
Conflicting revisions fail rather than silently overwriting another collaborator's newer edit.
Unknown, malformed or over-limit collaborative content fails closed.
nonClaims: This policy does not make user-generated content factually correct.
This policy does not replace human game-master judgement.
This policy does not certify a loopback-only preview for public internet deployment.
This policy does not make AI-generated narrative authoritative.
